readwrite/task: Some tasks turn one sequence into another of a different length. Translation, say: je suis étudiant becomes I am a student.
readwrite/enc: An encoder RNN reads the input, one token per step. Its final state sums up the whole sentence in a single vector.
readwrite/dec: A second RNN, the decoder, starts from that vector. It reads a start token and predicts the first word: I.
readwrite/feed: Each predicted word is fed back in to predict the next one: am, a, student.
readwrite/end: Until it predicts the end token. Four words, plus the end: five decoder steps.
train/tf: In training, the decoder reads the true previous word, not its own guess. That is teacher forcing: one early mistake cannot derail the rest of the sentence.
train/loss: Every step has a right answer, the next word of the target, so one sentence pair gives five predictions to score.
train/test: At test time there is no true word to read, so the decoder reads its own last prediction instead.
train/bottleneck: One weakness remains: everything about the input must squeeze through that one final vector, whether the sentence has three words or fifty.
